title: Inspect Robot Location Attributes in the Robotics Database
summary: A read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic for inspecting Robot Location records in the OptiSweep Robotics database and comparing the record with the corresponding RMS / fleet status UI location cue. Review station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when L2/L3 support needs to interpret a station or location in the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and associate it with a location shown in the RMS / fleet status UI.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify Robotics database records.
Do not use this procedure as a physical AGV recovery or E-stop procedure.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for a live database query or RMS location comparison; the packet does not provide a complete SSMS navigation path or SQL query.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) inspection and compare the record with the RMS / fleet status UI.
Review or assist when the Robot Location record is missing, cannot be associated with RMS, or contains blank or inconsistent identifying fields.

safety_notes: Do not modify database records as part of this diagnostic.
access_or_tools_needed: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) access to the OptiSweep Robotics database
RMS / fleet status UI access for location comparison

access_required: L2/L3 access to WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) on the support path
Access to the RMS / fleet status UI
system_preconditions: A relevant station or location has been identified for investigation.
The location can be identified by a station or workstation cue, if available, in RMS.

steps.title: Open the Robotics database in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.purpose: Establish a read-only view of the OptiSweep Robotics database that contains the Robot Location model/table.
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the OptiSweep Robotics database. Use read-only inspection and do not edit or execute changes against database records.
steps.expected_result: The OptiSweep Robotics database is selected and available for inspection in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
steps.healthy_condition: The Robotics database is accessible and its database objects can be inspected without making changes.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database is unavailable, inaccessible, or cannot be inspected read-only.

actions.label: Select Robotics database
actions.exact_action: Select the OptiSweep Robotics database in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the database cannot be accessed read-only.
Escalate to L3_support if the Robotics database is unavailable or access cannot be established.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The source identifies the Robotics database and describes the Robot Location database model/table.

steps.title: Locate the Robot Location record
steps.purpose: Find the live location record corresponding to the station or location under investigation.
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), locate the Robot Location database model/table and inspect the record for the relevant station or location. Use the available station or location identity to select the record; do not infer an unprovided table path or SQL query.
steps.expected_result: A Robot Location record corresponding to the investigated station or location is present and readable.
steps.healthy_condition: The record has an identifiable station or location identity that can be used for comparison with RMS.
steps.failure_condition: No relevant Robot Location record can be found, or the record lacks enough identifying information to associate it with the investigated location.

actions.label: Inspect Robot Location record
actions.exact_action: Locate the Robot Location database model/table and inspect the record for the relevant station or location.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the expected Robot Location record is missing.
Escalate if the record cannot be associated with the investigated location.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Robot Location database model/table contains information about locations, including station number and other location attributes.

steps.title: Inspect Robot Location attributes
steps.purpose: Determine the live configuration and state attributes associated with the investigated location.
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the Robot Location record fields for station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum number of AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
steps.expected_result: The live Robot Location record exposes readable values for station or location identity, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
steps.healthy_condition: The expected fields are populated and internally usable for identifying the location and interpreting its live occupancy, zone, type, capacity, and dwell-tracking configuration.
steps.failure_condition: One or more identifying or operational fields are blank, inconsistent, or unavailable.

actions.label: Review location fields
actions.exact_action: Check the station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum number of AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking field.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if identifying fields are blank or inconsistent.
Do not modify the record to correct a value during this diagnostic.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Robot Location model/table includes station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
Location types include sorter, tipper, hospital, shutdown, and GLD pre-queue locations.

steps.title: Compare the record with the RMS location cue
steps.purpose: Corroborate the database location identity against the live RMS / fleet status UI representation.
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI, locate the corresponding orange location or workstation ID and compare that live location cue with the station or location identity from the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robot Location record. Use the RMS location cue for association; do not assume that color alone proves a field value.
steps.expected_result: The Robot Location record can be associated with the corresponding RMS / fleet status UI location cue, including an orange location or visible workstation ID when present.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS / fleet status UI location cue and the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) record identify the same station or location.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS / fleet status UI cue cannot be matched to the database record, or the identifying values conflict.

actions.label: Compare RMS location
actions.exact_action: Compare the live record with the location being investigated in RMS, using orange locations and workstation IDs as visible location cues.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the database record cannot be associated with the RMS location.
Escalate if the RMS cue and database identifying fields are inconsistent.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The source describes orange locations shown in RMS and workstation IDs visible for stations.

success_criteria: The relevant Robot Location record is found in the OptiSweep Robotics database through WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
Station or location identity, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking are readable.
The database record can be associated with the corresponding RMS / fleet status UI location cue.
healthy_conditions: The Robotics database is accessible for read-only inspection.
The Robot Location record is present and identifiable.
The expected location attributes are populated and readable.
The WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) identity matches the corresponding RMS / fleet status UI station or location cue.
failure_conditions: The Robotics database or Robot Location model/table cannot be accessed.
The expected Robot Location record is missing.
Station or location identifying fields are blank or inconsistent.
The record cannot be associated with the RMS / fleet status UI location cue.
The database record would need to be modified to continue.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L2/L3 support when the expected Robot Location record is missing, cannot be associated with RMS, or contains blank or inconsistent identifying fields.
Do not modify database records during this diagnostic.
missing_details: The packet does not provide a dedicated Robot Location screenshot showing the requested fields; the available same-section frame is not a dedicated live Robot Location table view.
The packet does not provide an exact SSMS navigation path, database object path, or SQL query for locating the Robot Location record.
The packet does not provide a dedicated RMS map screenshot for the orange-location and workstation-ID comparison.
